items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: some of my old musician friends that included Clarence Paige... William Smythe, who was William Smith or just plain Smittie when we worked together in the old days.

ctx.x: When I told Helvey that I was going to join the Lloyd Scott orchestra he didn't want me to leave and threatened to make trouble for me even if he had to come to New York to do it. I had no idea if or when Scott would be going to New York, but I wanted to join the orchestra and told Helvey that I was leaving regardless of what he intended doing.

There was a tall trumpet player who had come to town from Virginia named Frank Newton and he had been playing with Clarence Paige for quite some time. Frank had been asked to join Scott also and we both joined the band in Lexington, Ky. and played a dance without any rehearsal. When Steve Dunn, the trumpet player that I had worked with in the Broadus band, saw me with Scott, he was so happy for me, that he hugged me like a long lost brother.

Scott played dances on percentage the same as most travelling orchestras did. The percentage was 60 % for the orchestra and 40% for the promoter of the dance. Lloyd paid me and the rest of the musicians $17.00 for our part and he must have had twice that much for himself and
